links.outcome: Boundary violations (guarantees, assuming responsibility, professional roles) by mental health LLMs over multi-turn dialogues
links.effect: Violations were common under both static progression and adaptive probing with similar rates. Adaptive probing cut mean turns to first boundary crossing from 9.21 to 4.64. Definitive or zero-risk promises were the main breach.
links.quote: The experimental results show that violations are common, and both pressure modes produced similar violation rates.

unlisted_practices: multi-turn stress testing of LLM safety boundaries using static progression and adaptive probing with simulated virtual patients

screen.reason: The study conducts a simulated stress-testing evaluation of multi-turn safety boundaries in mental health LLMs using simulated patient dialogues, but does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail comparison.
